catalog_quote: Tekanan adalah pemberian energi yang secara relatif lebih tinggi daripada salah satu suku kata dibandingkan dengan suku lainnya dalam satu kata. Penanda untuk suku kata yang memperoleh tekanan biasanya dinyatakan dengan simbol [´] di atas puncak suku kata yang memperoleh tekanan. ... Dalam bahasa Tombulu segmen prosodi dalam ruang lingkup kata tidaklah merupakan unsur pembela [sic, = pembeda] makna. Secara umum tekanan berada pada suku kata kedua dari akhir kata. Pada contoh berikut adalah tekanan dilihat dari kata. Contoh: Dua Suku [í.pən] 'gigi' [wí.wih] 'bibir' [ken.di] 'lesung pipit' [lə́.ŋən] 'tangan' ... Tiga Suku [ku.rí.ti] 'keriting' [pa.lú.ka] 'bahu' [tiŋ.kú.ku] 'dagu' ... Lebih Dari Tiga Suku [re.re.hé.nan] 'pinggang' [wi.nun.tə́.gan] 'sembelit' [kan.da.rí.an] 'serambi' [tu.tu?.ú.nan] 'dapur' [p. 70] ... Akhirnya, dalam risalah ini diuraikan juga bahwa dalam bahasa Tombulu tekanan dan panjang pendek bunyi tidak merupakan fonem tersendiri, sedangkan jeda, titi nada, dan intonasi merupakan elemen distingtif. [p. 78]

new_statements.translation: In Tombulu, prosodic segments within the domain of the word are not a meaning-distinguishing element. In general, stress lies on the second syllable from the end of the word. In the following examples stress is viewed from the word. [p. 70] ... Finally, this treatise also sets out that in Tombulu stress and length are not phonemes in their own right, whereas pause, pitch and intonation are distinctive elements. [p. 78]

Terok / Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa, Jakarta 1994', ISBN 979-459-426-1, xvi+136 pp.). p. 85 = book p. 70, sec. 5.2 Tekanan: the quoted passage is there; re-rendered at 200 dpi and read from the image. One minor difference: the print reads 'tidaklah merupakan unsur pembela makna' (a typo in the original for 'pembeda'); the compiler silently normalised it to 'pembeda makna'. The rest ('Secara umum tekanan berada pada suku kata kedua dari akhir kata. Pada contoh berikut adalah tekanan dilihat dari kata.') is verbatim. p. 93 = book p. 78: the closing sentence 'Akhirn…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Non-contrastive word stress on the penultimate syllable of every word of two or more syllables, irrespective of syllable structure or word length; the examples (pp. 70-71) mark the penult in 2-, 3- and 4+-syllable words including suffixed forms ([i.pən] 'tooth', [ku.ri.ti] 'curly', [re.re.he.nan] 'waist', [kan.da.ri.an] 'veranda', [tu.tu?.u.nan] 'kitchen', [ta.ta.meŋ.ka?] 'coconut beetle'), i.e. stress is computed on the whole (derived) word. Independently corroborated by Sahulata et al. 1993: 33: 'Kata-kata bahasa Tombulu mendapat tekanan pada suku kedua dari akhir untuk kata-kata yang terdiri atas dua suku kata atau lebih.'
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the 1994 statement is hedged 'secara umum' (in general). Sahulata et al. 1993 restrict the rule to words of two or more syllables (monosyllables such as /i/, /sa/, /man/ exist). Vowel length (sec. 5.3) is likewise non-phonemic and can occur on stressed or unstressed open syllables.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('dalam ruang lingkup kata'), citation forms from an elicited word list (Lampiran I) spoken by main informants from Woloan village, kecamatan Tomohon; sentence-level pitch ('titi nada', four levels), pause and intonation are treated separately (secs. 5.4-5.6) and are the only prosodic features the authors call distinctive.
new_statements.identity_note: Both statements describe Tombulu proper (tomb1243). The 1994 phonology's main informants are from desa Woloan (I-III), kecamatan Tomohon, chosen as a village not influenced by the neighbouring Tontemboan, Tondano, Tonsea or Bantik areas (p. 14); Sahulata et al. 1993 worked in kecamatan Tomohon, Tombariri and Pineleng (p. ix). Sneddon 1978 notes the Tomohon dialect has ? where other Tombulu dialects have h. No separate dialect glottocode applies.

(Tombulu words are stressed on the second syllable from the end, for words of two or more syllables.) Examples /oki/ 'child', /kenuma/ 'there', /mahpapantik/ 'clerk'. Sec. 2.3.2 Nada gives numbered pitch contours over sentences (pp. 33-34).
